themes.disagreements: Renal markers show high consistency in treatment prediction but lower, more variable support for outcome prognosis.
themes.interpretation: Candidates measuring kidney performance demonstrate strong predictive signals for treatment assignment and moderate signals for effect modification.
themes.name: Renal Function

themes.disagreements: Deconditioning shows strong signals across roles, whereas CRP level evidence is weak and lacks consistency.
themes.interpretation: Measures of general patient health, inflammation, and infection status provide evidence for both outcome prognosis and treatment effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Systemic and Clinical Status

themes.disagreements: Treatment and outcome signals are moderate, while the causal forest provides the strongest supporting signal for the effect modification role.
themes.interpretation: Blood pressure demonstrates a moderate relationship with treatment and outcome, coupled with a strong signal for effect modification.
themes.name: Hemodynamics

themes.disagreements: Cough productivity shows a moderate outcome signal but lacks the treatment or effect signals necessary for a confounder or modifier role.
themes.interpretation: Candidate measurements of cough characteristics and cranial nerve status show minimal or inconsistent evidence across all roles.
themes.name: Cough and Neurological Markers
